Subject: POC trial plan & model selection — GlobeCart

Hi Emma and Liam —

Thanks again for the productive call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the trial scope and success criteria. I’ve attached a short spreadsheet for success criteria and test dataset links.

High-level POC goal:
- Validate an LLM-based assistant for multilingual product title normalization and customer support triage for EN/ES/FR. Key constraints: < 500ms median generation latency for 512-token requests, < $0.015 per 1k tokens for inference cost on average, and parity with current rule-based extraction > 92% field-level accuracy.

Proposed evaluation plan (2-week trial):
1) Dataset & metrics (owner: GlobeCart ML / Liam)
   - 5k representative messages (mix EN/ES/FR), labeled for title normalization fields and triage intent.
   - Metrics: field-level accuracy, intent F1, output fluency (human spot-check), latency P50/P95, and estimated cost per 1k tokens.
2) Model selection (owner: Redwood SE / Markus + GlobeCart ML)
   - Primary candidate: Llama-2-13b-chat (quantized 4-bit variant for cost) — good instruction-following and decent multilingual coverage when finetuned/prompted.
   - Fallback candidate: Mistral-7B-Instruct (lower cost, faster latency; validate multilingual via prompts).
   - If multilingual coverage is insufficient: try Llama-2-70b-chat on Redwood Dedicated (if needed) as escalation.
3) Integration & infra (owner: GlobeCart infra + Redwood onboarding)
   - Network allowlist, test API keys, sample request templates. See attached network-config-template.pdf.
4) Timing & ownership
   - Kickoff: Tue Oct 13 (Redwood to provision test model endpoints by EOD Oct 13)
   - Week 1: run baseline runs against 1k samples, iterate prompts and config (batching/kv cache).
   - Week 2: full 5k run, quality review, cost/latency analysis, decision meeting on Oct 26.

Next steps
- Liam: share anonymized 1k seed dataset by EOD Oct 13.
- Emma: confirm procurement timeline and any NDA/procurement contacts (cced).
- Markus/Marissa/Ben: we’ll provision endpoints and baseline prompts; Markus will share recommended model/config (quantization, batch size, concurrency) by EOD Oct 13.

Attachments: GlobeCart-POC-success-criteria.xlsx, network-config-template.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Ben

Liam —

Great questions. Quick answers and a proposed baseline config: 

- Latency: our benchmarked latency numbers include only server-side inference (model forward) and tokenization; we recommend GlobeCart measure end-to-end latency including your pre/post-processing. For SLA purposes we can report both.

- Model recommendations:
  1) Llama-2-13b-chat (quantized int4) — Primary. Pros: strong instruction-following, lower development iteration friction. Cons: some languages underrepresented depending on domain; will need prompt tuning and a small finetune or RLHF step if you want deterministic normalizations.
  2) Mistral-7B-Instruct — Fallback. Pros: faster, cheaper. Cons: may need more prompt/context engineering for multilingual.
  3) If we see per-language gaps > 6-8%: propose short adaptation run on Llama-2-70b-chat or a small finetune on 13b using your labeled examples (we can estimate cost).

- Baseline endpoint config (what I’ll provision by EOD Oct 13):
  - Llama-2-13b-chat (quantized int4) — concurrency 8, batch size 4, max tokens 512, kv-cache enabled, response streaming off for batch runs.
  - Mistral-7B-Instruct — concurrency 16, batch size 8 for latency testing.

- Metrics we’ll report: per-language accuracy, per-language latency (P50/P95), cost per 1k tokens (inferred from token counts), and sample-level human pass rate (spot check).

I’ll attach a small README with prompt templates and the exact API calls we’ll use.

— Markus
